A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel convolutional network architecture for image captioning that incorporates both spatial and channel-wise attention mechanisms, and that the proposed SCA- CNN significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art image captioning approaches.

we propose to use spatial attention to model the spatial locations and channel-wise attention to model the feature channels, which are two important components of visual attention, and we show that this can significantly improve the performance on the task of image-to-sentence.
we introduce a novel visual attention mechanism that is spatial and channel-wise in a CNN, and that the proposed SCA architecture outperforms existing visual attention-based image-to-sentence models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spatial attention alone may be insufficient to fully exploit the rich information contained in the multi-layer feature maps of a CNN.
visual attention can be modeled as a dynamic feature extractor, which is channel-wise and multi-level.
the attention mechanism can be modeled at both spatial and channel-wise dimensions, and the proposed SCA- CNN is a general framework that can be applied to a variety of tasks beyond image captioning.
